title: The macro example in "What is A2UI?": raw results
what_this_is: Per-run figures from one test: draw the latest run of five GitHub workflows of the public repository a2uicatalog/a2ui as an isometric factory scene. Four ways of asking, 10 runs each, two models. Measured 9 November 2026; trimmed for publication 15 November 2026 from the demo's own results file. The message and patch bodies are left out.

lanes.macro: the model writes one call in Express (the SDK Express prompt with the macro inside it) and the server expands it
lanes.strict control: the model writes the whole components JSON, including the SVG itself; static; may not use style or use
lanes.lean control: the same, asked for a simpler scene; may use use; static
lanes.text-only list: a plain text list of the five workflows, no picture

prompt:
Draw the latest run of five GitHub workflows of the public repository a2uicatalog/a2ui as an isometric factory scene: five machines along a conveyor, in this order, one per workflow (read 2026-11-09T17:23:29Z). These five workflows are independent (different triggers); the scene is only a picture of their latest states, not one chained pipeline. The first stage is the latest commit (a commit has no run state); the check "registry-drift" is a weekly scheduled check of external registry listings, not a test of the commit.
Title: "Latest run of five a2uicatalog/a2ui workflows". Colour mood: teal.
Stages in order:
1. kind commit: name "c567e65", state latest
2. kind build: name "build-apps", state passed
3. kind check: name "registry-drift", state failed
4. kind package: name "pypi-publish", state passed
5. kind deploy: name "deploy", state passed
Also show one package crate on the conveyor at the first stage (the commit).

env.raster: headless, software raster (SwiftShader), a container, 2 CPUs
env.machine: Intel Xeon E5520 2.27 GHz, 4 cores, Debian 13 (a shared, loaded machine)
env.network: loopback (127.0.0.1), not a real network; the model API call itself goes over the internet and is inside the model time

facts.what: latest commit on the default branch (a commit has no run state)

"Network" is a loopback residual (127.0.0.1) and says nothing about a real network. The macro lane's first message is 36.8 KB (the static art and the numbers go over the wire once), the strict control's is 5.3 KB; after that a patch is 547 to 677 B on the wire. On a phone link the first message is the price of the later small patches.

Patches: every patch reloads the whole Image (median 5.7 ms to the Image load event, but about 170 ms until the next frame here, software raster: quote the second figure as patch-to-visible). Motion between patches is CSS inside the SVG (belt dashes, smoke, press, spinner, a crate that slides in); it restarts on every reload, which is why a crate that did not move is drawn in a separate static layer. Measured earlier (svg-pipeline spike, svg-sketch-agent): about 6 patches per second is the ceiling for a 63 KB image on this machine; this replay sends one every 3 s. Every replay step is a scripted what-if and is labelled so, including the caption text inside the surface. Reduced motion (tested, Chromium 153, a container without network): reduced motion is NOT honoured inside the image. The SVG contains a prefers-reduced-motion rule, but with the preference emulated the picture kept moving (two screenshots of the picture 800 ms apart differed, as they did without the preference), so the rule does not apply inside an SVG loaded through an Image here. The page's own replay does honour the preference: with it set, the replay does not autoplay (it stays on the real initial state with a Play button; without it, autoplay had reached what-if step 3 of 3 after 9 s). The way to stop the replay is Pause; the CSS motion inside the picture (belt dashes, smoke, press, spinner) cannot be stopped from the page. Other browsers were not tested.

Content-correct (every run of every lane, none dropped): the check reads the SVG string from the rendered Image's src (the decoded data URL), requires the image to have decoded (naturalWidth > 0), puts the string in a page and measures it. It checks five stages with the exact names in left-to-right order, each fully inside the viewBox, nonzero and with at least 4 visible shapes, exactly one active lamp in the exact state colour, a visible state word per stage with contrast of at least 4.5 against the pixels around it, a conveyor (id belt) spanning the stages, the crate nearest the first stage, no text under 12 px, nothing outside the canvas; the caption lists every name and state word; the macro call is compared with the spec; the patches are re-checked the same way. The text-only lane is checked for five lines with kind, name and state word and no Image. It does not judge looks beyond that: overlap or taste can still be poor in a content-correct run, and the image is parsed by the forgiving HTML parser, not the strict XML image decoder (the decode gate is naturalWidth).

Threshold disclosure: the minimum number of visible shapes per stage was 5 when the check was first written and was lowered to 4 AFTER the lean-control results were seen, because a compliant lean stage (one shared box reused with <use>, name, state word, lamp) has exactly 4 shapes. At 5, content-correct counts would be: Sonnet strict 9, lean 7, text-only 10; Haiku strict 5, lean 0, text-only 10 (macro unchanged). The change only helps the controls.

Contrast sampling: the state-word contrast is measured against the pixels around the word, with transparent pixels composited on the page card colour (light page). An earlier version of the check read transparent pixels as black and was fixed after review; all stored runs were re-checked offline. With the page in dark mode, runs with a state word under 4.5 contrast (not part of content-correct; the control SVGs do not adapt to dark mode): Sonnet strict 0 of 10, lean 1 of 10; Haiku strict 1, lean 9; macro 0 and 0.

Looking at the Haiku lean runs that the corrected check now passes (3 of 10: runs 1, 8 and 10) I disagree with the check on two of them: in run 10 the belt and boxes cover parts of several labels, and in run 1 labels overlap the belt and the crate, although the contrast measured around each word is fine (it samples the pixels around the text, not behind it). Run 8 is acceptable apart from the deploy label overlapping a lamp. So the 3 of 10 is a content-correct count, and by eye the Haiku lean control is poorer than that count suggests; the check was not changed for this.
